title: Standardized customer upgrade guidance pack: LTS + rolling releases
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Purpose: produce a reusable customer-facing 'upgrade guidance pack' that covers versioning language, LTS channel expectations, rollout gates, and step-by-step migration guidance for common breaking changes. This ticket delivers: (1) canonical release notes template for major/minor/patch and channel-specific notes (LTS vs rolling), (2) email + in-product comms templates with variable placeholders, (3) short migration guides for customers with dedicated/Dedicated-Private deployments, and (4) a support runbook for post-upgrade issues. This pack is intended for use by PMs, Release Engineers, and Customer Success when announcing or executing platform upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: One release-notes template for major releases and one for patch/patch-LTS, both with clear upgrade risk indicators and suggested migration steps
Email, status page, and in-product banner templates with merge variables ({{version}}, {{channel}}, {{impact}}, {{action_required}}, {{rollback_window}})
A migration checklist for at least three common breaking changes (KV cache format, default quantization profile change, runtime config semantics) with CLI commands and dry-run instructions
Support runbook that identifies metric thresholds and quick mitigation steps for rollbacks and partial rollouts
Templates reviewed and signed off by Eng (runtime), Security, and CS reps listed in comments
rollout_plan: Overview: adopt a gated rollout pattern by default for all non-patch LTS releases. Gate 0 (internal): CI + canary smoke on internal test accounts. Gate 1 (small external): 1% of eligible Dedicated/Dedicated-Private customers for 24h. Gate 2 (broad external): 25% for 48h. Gate 3 (full): 100% after 7 days of stable metrics. Metrics to monitor: error_rate (5xx API errors), median_latency (p95), token_cost_delta, key_user_jobs_failed. Rollback criteria: error_rate > 3x baseline sustained > 30 minutes OR p95 latency increase > 2x baseline with customer-impacting errors. Communication cadence: pre-release notice (7d), day-of release note, canary status update (24h), progressive updates at each gate, post-release summary with known issues and remediation steps. Escalation path: on-call engineer -> runtime lead -> PM -> CS lead. Automate gate enforcement using release-controller flags and ensure manual override is auditable.
comms_templates: email_subject_major: 'Redwood Inference: Major runtime release {{version}} (LTS) – Action recommended by {{release_date}}'

email_body_major: 'Hi {{customer_name}},

We will begin rolling out Redwood runtime {{version}} to your account on {{release_date}}. This is a {{channel}} release with LTS support for {{lts_window}}. Summary: {{one_line_summary}}. Impact: {{impact}}. Action required: {{action_required}} (examples: restart services, run migration utility, verify prompts). Suggested timeline: backup config -> dry-run migration -> apply -> verify. If you are on Dedicated/Private and prefer coordinated scheduling, reply to this email or open a support ticket referencing {{release_ticket}}.

We recommend running the provided migration dry-run and validating your prompt regressions against the evaluation suite attached. See the migration guide: {{migration_doc_url}}.

If you have strict maintenance windows, let us know and we will coordinate.

Thanks,
Redwood Release Team'
email_subject_patch: 'Redwood runtime patch {{version}} rolling out – no customer action expected'

status_page_template: 'Incident-type: planned-maintenance; Impact: {{impact}}; Start: {{start}}; End: {{end}}; Description: Rolling deployment of runtime {{version}} across regions. No action required unless flagged in personalized message. For updates see: {{status_link}}'
in_product_banner: 'Planned: Redwood runtime upgrade to {{version}} on {{release_date}}. Possible short interruptions for some Dedicated/private customers. Click for details: {{migration_doc_url}}'

support_runbook_summary: 'Step 1: Confirm customer environment and channel. Step 2: Check gate metrics dashboards (errors/latency/cost). Step 3: If criteria breached, engage rollback via release-controller (rollback flag) and notify customer. Step 4: If partial failure, provide targeted mitigation (repoint to model variant, increase capacity, or schedule hotfix). Contact list: runtime-oncall, lead-release-engineer, cs-eng liaison.'
migration_guide_outline: Objective: deliver concise migration instructions and a safe dry-run path. Sections: 1) Quick risk summary (what changes and why) 2) Pre-upgrade checklist (backups, eval suite, contact points) 3) Dry-run commands (CLI examples) 4) Post-upgrade verification (queries, latency checks, token-cost comparison) 5) Rollback instructions. Example CLI usage: redwood-upgrade --version {{version}} --dry-run --target ACCOUNT_ID --output report.json ; to apply: redwood-upgrade --version {{version}} --apply --target ACCOUNT_ID ; to rollback: redwood-release-controller rollback --deployment {{deployment_id}}. Notes for common breaking changes: KV cache format change requires cache-warmup step: run 'redwood-cache migrate --from-format v1 --to-format v2 --dry-run' then warm with representative requests. Quantization profile upgrades: verify model outputs on a designated evaluation prompt set and compare embedding similarity with tolerance thresholds. Runtime config semantics (timeout/batching): validate that new defaults do not push latency above p95 SLO by running load-profile scripts in controlled staging. Include sample troubleshooting commands and grepable log snippets for faster triage.
